opener_episode.title: The Friendliest Store in the Mall | Ron Johnson Built the Apple Store
opener_episode.why: Most recent confirmed new interview and the closest thematic match: Johnson's 'physical retail is not dying' thesis is the mirror of Avery's 'Click & Mortar' model (social-first marketing + curated physical pop-ups), so the opener can say 'your conversation with Ron Johnson about why physical retail isn't dying...' and pivot straight to the art version.

angles.headline: Click & Mortar: what the Apple Store lesson looks like in the art world
angles.pitch: Avery explains how he launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries, scaled it to eight figures a year, and coined 'Click & Mortar' by pairing social-first marketing with curated physical pop-ups.
angles.builds_on: Ron Johnson episode (2026-09-16) on physical retail and customer experience

angles.headline: How to build an artist into a brand: the Alec Monopoly playbook
angles.pitch: A 'choose yourself' story of developing a street artist into a global brand with sold-out shows from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, without waiting for the traditional gallery system's permission.
angles.builds_on: Show's core reinvention/'choose yourself' theme and its creative-career guests (e.g., Nancy Cartwright)

angles.headline: Art as an asset: what the rich actually buy and why
angles.pitch: The dealer who advises celebrities, athletes and HNW collectors (Kris Jenner, Scott Disick placements reported by Us Weekly and Page Six) on how art fits into wealth, and the outlandish requests that come with it.
angles.builds_on: Joseph Moore episode (2026-08-27) on how the rich stay rich
